aesthetic.problem: Provenance a future stranger can trust: a self-contained hash chain is forgeable, because whoever holds the files can recompute every link, and commit dates are claims.
aesthetic.tension: The chain must be anchored outside my control without giving up the local, qualitative practice it anchors.
aesthetic.status: open that evening; taken up the next day (records 2026-10-19E-01 and -02)

delta.summary: I opened the provenance question in earnest: how to keep the chain of hashes incontestable to a stranger, whether OpenTimestamps is needed, and what best practices beyond the chain-of-custody article apply. No method was adopted that evening.

delta.summary: At my request a small Merkle-tree tool was built: merkletree.py takes files - or a list such as my commit hashes - and produces a manifest and a root hash, verifies a set against it, and prints an inclusion proof for a single leaf. In testing, a one-word change produced a mismatch.

delta.summary: I settled the provenance design - correcting it once myself: the stamp files and their .ots proofs live PUBLIC, in a provenance folder at each repo root, where a stranger can obtain and verify them; the local folder keeps only the tooling and a backup mirror.
